issues.legal_issue: Tax liability arising from taxable transactions constitutes arrears for allocation between successor States even before assessment quantifies the amount due.
material_facts: The dealer made sales of manganese ore during a period spanning the reorganisation of the State, including sales from districts transferred to another State.
The tax authorities assessed the dealer after the reorganisation for sales made during the relevant period.
The High Court quashed the composite assessment on the basis that tax could not be in arrears before assessment proceedings determined the amount due.
The Supreme Court considered whether the liability for tax depended on its quantification by assessment.
issues.conclusion: For the purpose of section 78 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, arrears means dues or amounts that have become due by way of tax; the liability does not depend on assessment proceedings or quantification. The High Court’s judgment was set aside and the matter remanded for decision of the remaining issues.
issues.legal_principle: Section 78 allocates the right to recover arrears of taxes other than taxes on property to the successor State in whose territory the place of assessment is included. Sections 78 and 83 together address tax recovery and refunds, while section 91 is residuary. A tax liability arises when taxable sales or purchases occur, although enforcement awaits assessment and quantification; the liability is independent of assessment. The Court relied on Kedarnath Jute Mfg. Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Calcutta, [1972] 1 S.C.R. 277.

predicates.state_reorganisation_tax_allocation_appe: The proceeding concerns allocation between successor States of the right to recover tax following a reorganisation of a State.
predicates.taxable_transactions_occurred: A dealer made sales or purchases that were subject to tax.
predicates.tax_amount_not_yet_quantified: The tax liability had not yet been quantified through assessment when the allocation question arose.

issues.definition: When a State-reorganisation tax-allocation appeal concerns taxable transactions whose liability has not yet been quantified, the liability counts as arrears.

issues.legal_issue: Tax amounts arising from taxes other than taxes on property are governed by the provisions specifically addressing tax recovery and refunds, rather than the residuary allocation provision.
material_facts: The dispute concerned allocation of sales-tax recovery rights between States following reorganisation.
The statutory scheme separately addressed recovery of tax arrears and liability to refund taxes, and also contained a residuary provision for assets and liabilities not otherwise addressed.
issues.conclusion: Amounts due by way of tax are not covered by the residuary provision in section 91; sections 78 and 83 govern the allocation relevant to taxes other than taxes on property.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 78 and 83 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 specifically address recovery of tax arrears and liability to refund taxes, respectively, by reference to the successor State containing the place of assessment. Section 91 applies residually to assets and liabilities not dealt with by the preceding provisions.

predicates.state_reorganisation_asset_allocation: The proceeding concerns allocation of assets or liabilities between States following reorganisation.
predicates.tax_other_than_property: The amount at issue arises from a tax other than a tax on property.
predicates.tax_specific_allocation_provisions_exist: The statutory allocation scheme contains provisions specifically addressing recovery or refund of the tax.

issues.definition: In a State-reorganisation allocation proceeding, amounts arising from a non-property tax covered by specific tax-allocation provisions are excluded from residuary allocation.
